title: The King's Chessman
subtitle: Nassington Walk
welcome_text: [[c:A mystery walk around Nassington, where a royal hall once stood and King Cnut is said to have feasted and played chess.]]
start_text: [[c:Start at the Black Horse Inn on Fotheringhay Road.]]

coins.explain: [[c:You have a purse of 5 coins for the whole walk. Hints are free. Showing an answer costs coins.]]

layers.label: Mystery story
layers.description: [[c:The story and the puzzles. Switch it off for a history-only walk.]]

route.name: Church Street and the village hall
route.label: Village hall

route.name: St Mary the Virgin and All Saints Church
route.label: Church

story: [[c:Nassington, about the year 1020. King Cnut is staying at his royal hall by the church, with his court and his bishops.]]
[[c:Every night the King plays chess, and his favourite piece is a carved walrus-ivory king. This morning it is gone.]]
[[c:Four people were in the hall: Ulf, a Danish guard; Edith, the hall cook; Brother Aldred, a bishop's clerk; and Orm, a travelling poet. Find the chessman before the King loses his temper.]]

start_page.title: Getting to the start
start_page.intro: [[c:The walk starts and finishes at the Black Horse Inn.]]
parking: [[c:Parking: please park considerately on the village streets, or ask at the pub. If you're driving, park first and then open the walk.]]
start_page.support: [[c:Support the village: Nassington has two pubs, the Black Horse and the Queen's Head. The walk takes about 1 hour to 1 hour 30.]]

lengths.label: [[c:Short walk: Church Street loop]]
lengths.description: [[c:Along Church Street to the church and the Prebendal Manor, back on the field path south of the village.]]

lengths.label: [[c:Medium walk: round the village]]
lengths.description: [[c:Adds St Mary's Close and the Queen's Head, going round the west and north of the village.]]

lengths.label: [[c:Long walk: the southern fields]]
lengths.description: [[c:A countryside loop south across the fields before coming back through the village to the north end.]]

medium:4-5: [[c:Take the footpath south from the Prebendal Manor, turn right along the field path and follow it round the west of the village to Apethorpe Road. Turn right along the pavement, then go up St Mary's Close. About 900 metres.]]
short:4-7: [[c:Take the footpath south from the Prebendal Manor, then turn left along the field path east to Station Road. Turn left and walk back up to the Black Horse. About 770 metres.]]

lengths_note: Route colours: short green, medium copper, long blue. legs = path along real roads/paths between consecutive stops (from OpenStreetMap).
